content: A pendant group, also known as a side group, refers to a molecular group that is attached to the backbone chain of a larger molecule. Typically, this larger molecule is a polymer. For instance, in a polystyrene chain, the phenyl groups serve as the pendant groups. When pendant groups are large and bulky, such as adamantyl groups, they tend to increase the glass transition temperature (Tg) of the polymer. This occurs because these bulky groups hinder the polymer chains from sliding past one another easily, thereby restricting molecular mobility. Conversely, short alkyl pendant groups can have the opposite effect. They may reduce the glass transition temperature by acting as a lubricant, facilitating easier movement of the polymer chains.
